raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. I know what this soil wants, and I know what will sell. I do not read, but I have watched this land for fifty years. I know what my mother grew, and her mother before her.

I will grow **winter wheat** and **summer maize** — the same rotation everyone here does, the same rotation I have always done. I have about 4 mu of land I can still manage at my age, especially since my son is in the city now. After the wheat comes out in June, I put maize in the same ground. Two crops, one piece of land, one year.

For wheat seed, I will buy the common improved variety from the village shop — I do not save my own seed anymore, the shop seed yields better. For maize, I always buy hybrid seed, the same kind my neighbor uses — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has. Hybrid maize is just what everyone buys now.

For fertilizer, I spread what I always spread. The man at the agro-shop tells me how much. I use more nitrogen than maybe I need — I worry about the plants going yellow. I hire the tractor for tillage before planting wheat. For maize after the wheat harvest, I use rotary tillage again before seeding.

Water I pump from the well — four times for wheat through the cold season and heading, two or three times for maize in the summer. Summer rains help with the maize.

I spray for weeds and bugs when I see problems, or when my neighbor says there is something going around. Two or three times for wheat, once or twice for maize.
